changes.was: Kin plans Thanksgiving so you don't have to.
changes.now: Kin plans the family gathering so you don't have to.
changes.why: Thanksgiving isn't observed in Nigeria, so the occasion needs to be a general family gathering instead.

changes.was: Who's bringing pie, who's picking up Grandma, when the turkey goes in.
changes.now: Who's bringing the food, who's picking up Grandma, when everyone arrives.
changes.why: No curated guidance exists for specific Nigerian family occasion customs, so details are kept general rather than invented.
The brief requires stating the 14-day trial length wherever 'free' appears.

changes.was: Kin plans Thanksgiving so you don't have to.
changes.now: Kin plans Christmas so you don't have to.
changes.why: Thanksgiving isn't celebrated in the UK; Christmas is the equivalent family logistics moment.
Free trial length must be stated wherever 'free' appears.
"Sorted" is the everyday local word for something dealt with, while "handled" reads as imported American phrasing.

changes.was: Kin plans Thanksgiving so you don't have to. Who's bringing pie, who's picking up Grandma, when the turkey goes in. Handled.
changes.now: Kin plans the WhatsApp group so you don't have to. Who's bringing the drinks, who's fetching Gran, when to leave. Sorted.
changes.why: Thanksgiving and its customs (pie, turkey) are American and unfamiliar in South Africa, so the chore is reframed around the WhatsApp group, the dominant local reference.
The brief requires the 14-day trial length to be stated wherever 'free' appears.

flags.text: Check: The CTA uses 'free' but doesn't state the 14-day trial length as required by the mandatories.

Check: 'family gathering' with Grandma-pickup and food-bringing evokes wedding/naming-ceremony style occasions (owambe). There's no snapshot guidance on referencing these, so tread carefully with assumptions about family structure.
Check: Generic 'family gathering' misses a chance to use locally recognisable life-admin chores (BVN/NIN, prepaid electricity, generator fuel) that would land harder with this audience.

Check: Swapping 'Thanksgiving' for 'Christmas' is right, but the details (pie, Grandma, turkey) are Thanksgiving-specific staples, not typical British Christmas admin. This reads like a partial localisation.
Check: 'pie' and 'turkey' together, without British Christmas markers (Boxing Day, crackers, in-laws visiting), may still feel imported rather than native life-admin chores.
Check: 'Kin plans the WhatsApp group' implies Kin reads or accesses group chat messages, which may trigger distrust about personal message access unless purpose and control are made clear.
Check: The master copy doesn't claim Kin manages a WhatsApp group; this variant introduces a new capability (accessing/organising group chats) not present in the US master.
Check: 'fetching Gran' swaps a US family reference for a UK/SA-style term; confirm this doesn't read as assuming a particular family/household structure.
